title: Rina's Wobbly Shoes
markdown:
The sunbeams were painting the path a warm bright gold, like spilled honey. Rina the rabbit hopped along. Hop, hop, hop. Her brand-new shiny red shoes felt absolutely perfect on her furry little feet. They made her feel as if she could hop right up, up, up, all the way to the moon.

"These shoes are the bestestest shoes in the whole world," she whispered, her little pink nose twitching. A gentle breeze tickled her whiskers, and the air smelled sweet with happy daisies. It was a wonderfully happy afternoon, the kind that makes you want to wiggle and giggle.

Then — snap. One shiny buckle went wobbly. Clunk-wobble-trip. Her foot went sideways. The happy hop became a stumble. Her tummy flip-flopped.

"How will I hop home now? My feet feel wonky." One tiny step was like walking on jelly. Wibble-wobble.

A dewdrop of a worry had almost arrived when a tiny buzzy sound came from under a yellow dandelion.

"Buzz-buzz-buzz. A bit of a wobble-tumble?"

Cobb the cobbler beetle scuttled out, a little magnifying glass on his nose. He was famous in the meadow for fixing things, with a cheerful buzz and a clickety-click of six speedy legs.

"Hello, fluffy friend. Trouble with the fabulous footwear. Do not worry your head. Cobb is on the case. Buzz-buzz-buzz."

Rina showed Cobb the broken buckle, still shiny, still almost new. Cobb peered through his glass, his little beetle eyes looking very serious. "Aha. A classic case of buckle-breakage. Fear not, my dear Rina. I have just the thing to make it strong again." He scurried off, as quick as a blink, and came back with a long strong strand of sparkly spider silk. "This will hold it tight, tighter than a tick on a sheep."

He tied it. Rina tried a small hop. The silk stretched like a rubber band and boinged her foot up. "Whee. Very bouncy. A trampoline for my foot." The shoe did a jig all by itself.

Cobb scratched his head with a tiny leg. "A little too much boing." Therefore he tried again: a plump red berry, smeared with enthusiasm. "Berry glue. Super-duper sticky."

Rina stepped. Squelch. Her foot stuck. She pulled. Pop. The shoe looked wonderfully, deliciously red. "My shoe is very yummy-looking now. It smells like a sweet treat."

Cobb's belly shook. "Berries are better for eating, I suppose."

Rina felt sillier and wobblier. Her hops were only stumbles. But Cobb kept buzzing up new ideas, antennae wiggling.

"What if we do not only fix it? What if we make it better? Super-special?" He gathered a coiled daisy-spring like a little metal worm, soft moss like a green pillow, and a smooth grey pebble. "We shall invent the marching shoe."

He worked clickety-quick: spring where the buckle had been, moss on the sole, pebble on top like a proud button.

Rina slipped her foot in. Light. Springy. Soft. A step went boing. The moss made it quiet. The pebble went tap-tap-tap. She tried a proper Rina hop. Boing-tap. Boing-tap. Not a wobble. A marching hop, like a happy parade of one.

"It is even better. I can march all the way home." She wiggled her nose thanks. Cobb held his antennae high. "Any time. We beetles find a way. Buzz-buzz-buzz."

And Rina, with her perfectly marching bouncy tap-tap-tapping shoes, hopped merrily down the golden path, feeling brave and wonderfully sure, her floppy ears bouncing with every cheerful boing-tap all the way home, where the door knew her by the sound.
characters: Rina (rabbit in new red shoes), Cobb (cobbler beetle)
author: StoryGen Community
